brief: Goldman's Miller argues scarce growth makes growth composition matter more. Durable compounders should beat high-growth cyclicals as Fed tightening, oil near $100 and 10-year yields above 5% weigh on momentum names. The AI-over-cyclicals call is working and GS still likes it. At the index level equities grind higher only because the AI trade props up the tape. Rate-sensitive pockets have sold off (homebuilders -17.5% in 3 months, non-profitable tech -11.4% since July, lending-sensitive equities underperforming), though softer PCE/NFP prints are pushing yields lower and pushing out the next Fed hike, which could relieve those pockets if sustained. Datacenter power demand forecasts (108GW by 2030) stay intact despite IPP and gas-infrastructure de-ratings. Japan outperforms on AI leadership plus gradual BoJ normalization and a new $140bn datacenter push. In France, OAT-Bund spreads near 150bps are spreading to BTPs. GS would buy EU bank dips only if French risk stays contained. China's Golden Week data and a widening production-consumption gap are the swing factor for European luxury. A Bolsonaro win is seen bullish for Brazil rate-sensitive equities. The AI/non-AI split holds only until midterms, which GS calls probably not risk-positive, forces one cost of capital onto the whole tape.
